subject: Pilot credit mechanics & operator license swap — on-prem pricing path
messages:
From: Samir Amin <samir@clearskyhealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment pricing — pilot credit & operator license question

Monica,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team (engineering + security) liked the runtime perf. Before we take an internal procurement + architecture pass, two quick commercial questions:

1) Pilot credits: will Redwood provide a token/compute credit to run a 6-week pilot that includes load testing (burst to 150k tokens/day)? If so, what are the mechanics (one-off credit, invoice credit on conversion, or refund)?

2) Operator license swap: we typically buy operator licenses (per-operator) to manage on-prem infra. If we commit to a 12-month dedicated VPC, would Redwood consider swapping operator licenses for a node-credit or reserved-node equivalence? That would help our internal budget lines.

We also need a rough mapping of support tiers (response times and included hours) because our Security/Privacy team will gate the SOW on a named on-call/response SLA.

Attached is a short MAP (high-level requirements). Looking for a quick commercial path so procurement can prioritize.

—Samir Amin
Head of Platform, ClearSky Health
Attachments: CSH-MAP-v1.xlsx

-----Original Message-----

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Samir Amin <samir@clearskyhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing — pilot credit & operator license question

Samir — great to hear the team found the demo helpful. Short answers upfront:

• Pilot credits: Yes — we can do a time-boxed pilot credit model. Typical approach: we issue an invoice credit for pilot usage that applies if you convert within 30 days of pilot close; otherwise it expires. We can also do a refundable pilot deposit for high-burst tests if you prefer.

• Operator license swap: We can map operator licenses to reserved-node credits on a one-time conversion at a negotiated rate (example: 1 operator license ≈ 0.25 reserved-node-months for standard operator functions). Need to confirm exact mapping with engineering/finance.

• Support tiers: see summary below (I can send the official SLA exhibit):
  - Standard: 8x5 email support, 24-48h response for Sev 1, no named on-call.
  - Business: 24x7 monitoring, 4h response Sev 1, 2 named SRE contacts, 40 included SRE hours/month.
  - Enterprise: 24x7 priority, 1h response Sev 1, named on-call rotation, 120 included SRE hours/month + runbook support.

Ill loop Jordan (sales lead) and Marissa (solutions) to draft a short commercial play: pilot credit amount, conversion mechanics, and an operator-swap proposal. Can you confirm desired pilot window (start date), and whether ClearSky prefers a refundable deposit or invoice credit model?

Best,
Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Amin <samir@clearskyhealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot credit mechanics & operator license swap — on-prem pricing path

Samir / Monica — thanks for the context. Putting a concrete option on the table to help procurement move quickly. Outline below is negotiable; opening position intended to minimize approval friction.

Proposal (Option A — pilot-credit + operator-swap):
• Pilot: 6-week pilot, capped at 200k tokens/day (to cover burst). Pilot credit = $18,000 (invoice credit applied on signed 12-month commitment within 45 days of pilot end). If ClearSky opts not to convert, credit expires; refundable deposit option also available for additional $2k admin refundable if full conversion happens.
• Operator license swap: We propose a conversion matrix in the SOW: every 4 operator licenses = 1 reserved-node-month (r-node-month) at standard sku equivalence. For a 12-month commitment, we’ll count the up-front conversion as a prepay credit against the first 3 months of reserved capacity. Exact conversion will be validated in the SOW and capped per-site.
• Platform fee: For this deal we offer a one-time platform-fee waiver for the first 6 months if you sign the 12-month committed r-node purchase within 30 days of pilot end. This is timebound and conditioned on a moderate usage floor (to prevent costless abuse).
• Support: Business tier included for the first 3 months; Enterprise tier can be purchased at a 25% discount if added at contract signature.

Attachments: draft pilot SOW and conversion table (pilot-SOW-draft.pdf).

Next steps: If this looks directionally OK, Monica can send a redline-friendly SOW and we can route a commercial term sheet to procurement. If procurement prefers invoice-credit vs refundable deposit, well honor the invoice-credit model by default.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Principal Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----

From: Samir Amin <samir@clearskyhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearskyhealth.com
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot credit mechanics & operator license swap — on-prem pricing path

Jordan / Monica — thanks for the quick turnaround. The proposal is clear and aligns with what procurement needs. A couple small asks before we route to legal/finance: 

1) Can the platform-fee waiver be scoped to just the pilot site (we have multiple sites) instead of a global waiver? That will make internal approval easier.
2) For the operator license conversion, can we get an example calculator in the SOW showing real numbers for our estate (we currently have 16 operators across 3 sites)? Seeing the conversion math will help procurement approve the mapping.

If you send the redlineable SOW + the example conversion sheet, Ill push this to legal and loop finance. Were hopeful to get procurement sign-off in 10 business days if the SOW aligns.

—Samir
Head of Platform, ClearSky Health
